implementerProof.how: Of the proofs the implement handoff carries at ef448091, I drove the same surfaces independently from my own builds in the round before this one and found each as it reported: acceptance A5 over the HTTP API on ten LINUX specs, base main 2d3a725f against head ef448091, with a control run on each side rather than only on the base; and four of the six alternating replay runs of my own A1 (base 411.68 / 402.18, head 380.50 / 383.06 CPU-seconds, every one of the four with saturated false, 174 writes sent, 0 failed, end state aa48884b08c5 and box_busy_before 1.2-1.6%). A re-pin drain replaced this pod with the fifth and sixth runs outstanding and took the whole load-test root with it, so those four runs' step directories, their profiles and A5's recorded records are gone; the figures above are what I reported to the architect as I measured them, not files I can still show. This round reached no new measurement: the head is unrunnable for the two reasons in failures, so starting a six-hour measurement on it would have measured a head that must change.

failures.criterion: A8, required checks green at the head: the head carries a CI verdict at all.
failures.evidence: The head has no CI run of any kind. `gh api repos/sjawhar/legion/commits/<sha>/check-runs --jq .total_count` is 0 at the code head e4118455e7becb6f3b6036ffde8bdc87900e1fa5 and 0 at the branch head af34d101df3ba2c7edc749f60926221881cd2646, and `gh run list --branch legion/INFRA-646` lists nothing newer than ef448091's run 41061824411. The cause is in the push: it carried code and a handoff together - `jj diff --from 9e5dd9c1 --to af34d101 --name-only` is packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/pmdoc/splice.go and .legion/INFRA-646/implement.json - while its head commit af34d101's message ends with `skip-checks: true` after two empty lines, so GitHub started no workflow for the push. skill://legion-worker names this exactly: a push whose commits touch only .legion/<issue>/ carries that line and no other push does, the daemon classifies a push by its paths and never by the trailer, and a trailered code push gets no verdict carried, so a head with no CI is one a base that requires a check will not merge. The remedy is the rewrite path of skill://legion-worker/references/conflicts-and-rewrites.md: describe the head again without that line, `jj bookmark set legion/INFRA-646 -r @- --allow-backwards`, then push once, so the code head gets a run; a rewrite head is a code push and never carries the line.

failures.criterion: A8, required checks green at the head: the branch carries main's fixes for the lanes that are red on it.
failures.evidence: The branch lacks two commits that are on main and that fix the lanes which failed its last complete run. Checked at 05:20Z, not taken on report: `jj log -r 'cd9b50df5 & ::main@origin'` and the same for 7d12a8715 both answer, so cd9b50df583d (test(dispatch): the route pin counts the app-installation route, #2551) and 7d12a871592e (ci: the listener server-change job's filter covers the Dispatch api testdata, #2552) are on main; `jj log -r 'cd9b50df5 & ::e4118455e7becb6f3b6036ffde8bdc87900e1fa5'` and the same for 7d12a8715 answer nothing, so neither is an ancestor of the code head. The last complete run on this branch, 41061824411 at ef448091, failed envoy-go, envoy-go-race and ci-filters, and ci-ok with them; ci-ok is now required, so the same three sink the merge when CI does run. This is a need only the base meets, which is one of the three cases skill://legion-worker/references/conflicts-and-rewrites.md allows a forward merge for, and the architect has directed it (Envoy, 2026-10-31T05:18:29Z). Merge main, push without the skip-checks line, and the round runs on that head.

observations: What this round did establish, before the pod went: the defect I reported at 01:04Z is fixed and the fix is exactly one word. pmdoc/splice.go:102 read `wantsDocument("BlockIndex")`, naming a function the cutover commit had deleted, and now reads `wantsDocument("BlockIndexes")`; `jj diff -r e4118455 --name-only` is that one file and the hunk is that one line. The red test that pinned it is the branch's own, TestTheZeroValidDocumentWantsADocument/BlockIndexes at valid_methods_test.go:101, so I wrote none. It had failed in both Go lanes of run 41061824411 - envoy-go exit 123 with pmdoc at 315.2 s, envoy-go-race with pmdoc at 1290.0 s - while lint, test and pr-title were green, which is how a defect in the changed package reached the tester with the required set passing.

A5 at base 2d3a725f against head ef448091, reported to the architect at 01:01Z and accepted by it: 972 records a side over twelve writes a spec on ten LINUX specs through the HTTP API, every status equal and all 522 markdown SHA-256s equal. I ran four drives rather than three, so there is a control on each side: base-against-base differs in 576 (record, field) positions, head-against-head in 576, base-against-head in 579. The three positions base-against-head carries that neither same-build control does are one field, opened_event_id, on LINUX-186's ask and the two later reads that list it, 32456 at base against 32457 at head, stable across two runs a side. I took it into the database rather than guessing: the event multisets are identical at 157 events, every one of the ten issues' own event log is identical in order and content, and the only difference is the cross-issue interleaving of a deferred artifact.human_edited of an earlier spec landing sooner on the faster build. The architect ruled at 01:02Z to record it and not block, since the per-issue log is the contract. One caution on my own method: my first base dump read 155 events with two artifact.human_edited missing and I nearly recorded a semantic difference; a dump sixty seconds later read 157 with the same ten, so it was the settlement tail, not the change.

The fingerprints, for the carry rule the architect gave at 01:04Z: ef448091 is 81715b4d5a9d994a4eca60cc036c75271f12619d5fc5489e681c00a967dd9e5c and both e4118455 and af34d101 are 2d27ff8b9eeacc869d89d7ce06d631674ffe7a16755d11c91b8ca8bb361aa1dc. They differ, as the one-word fix makes them, and the ruling was that the results taken at ef448091 carry to the fix head provided the diff is that one string plus handoffs, which it is. A forward merge of main will move the fingerprint again and that ruling will need restating for the merged head.

Two re-pin drains have now replaced this pod mid-measurement. Nothing of a run survives one: the load-test root, its Postgres, the restored replay seed and every prepared template are rebuilt from nothing, about forty minutes before the first write, and a six-run A1 is four and a half hours after that. The next round on the merged head starts from an empty disk again. Evidence that must outlive a drain goes to a Dispatch artifact as it is produced, not at the end.
